paragraphs: Children in Enfield's care live with carers approved by the council's own fostering service or by independent agencies such as the services shown above. The council's fostering statement of purpose for 2024 to 2027 says it tries to keep children close to their families, friends, schools and GP, and that finding carers who live in or close to the borough remains a priority. Recruitment now runs through the North London Fostering Hub, hosted by Camden, which brings Enfield together with Barnet, Camden, Hackney, Haringey and Islington to recruit and support more carers across the area; it launched on 1 October.

Enfield's draft strategy for looked after children for 2023 to 2028, published for consultation in February 2023, gives a picture of local need. The council was caring for 396 children and young people on 31 March 2022, and around 65% of children in its care were in foster homes in 2020. Young people aged 10 to 15 made up 35% of children in care and those aged 16 and over 30%, and 46% were living outside the borough, which is why the council wants more carers locally and has helped existing carers add bedrooms through loft conversions and extensions.

The council's fostering pages say which children most need homes: brothers and sisters who should stay together, teenagers, babies and children under two, disabled children, young people on remand aged 10 to 17, and young parents with their babies. Carers are approved for short-term and long-term fostering, with Staying Put possible up to 21, respite, parent and child, and family and friends care.

Enfield welcomes enquiries from anyone over 21 who lives in the UK, including single people and unmarried couples, and offers a one-to-one conversation with one of its foster carers. Preparation is a four-day Skills to Foster programme; approved carers get a named supervising social worker, four training events a year, development days, support groups and paid Fostering Network membership. Pay is a weekly maintenance allowance plus a skills fee in five age bands, with birthday, festival and holiday allowances; the council does not publish the amounts, so ask it and two or three of the services above for their figures. Nearby, see our pages for Barnet, Haringey, Waltham Forest, Hertfordshire and London.
